title: 47:1 sit in the dust. Those who sat in the dust to do their work were the slaves. As a slave, Babylon is forced to grind meal with hand stones, to remove her veil and expose herself to public view, to immodestly "make bare the leg" (47:2) so that her skirts don't obstruct her work, and so forth. It is also likely that slaves were poorly dressed and thus inadequately covered. Sitting in the dust was also a sign of mourning (3:26; Lam. 2:10; Ezek. 26:15-17). This passage refers both to the captivity of the literal Babylon and Chaldea (seen through the eyes of prophecy) and to the loss of freedom and power suffered by those who belong to spiritual Babylon, which is the wicked world (contrast with 52:2).
author: Tina M. Peterson
